note: Shipped under the 2026-09-01 FALLBACK. (1) LANGUAGE: the study was run in Spain using the Spanish LOT-R of Ferrando, Chico & Tous (2002, Psicothema 14(3), 673-680), per the postprint's Measures section. The administered Spanish is not recoverable within the scoped sources: the Study 3 CSV has bare column names and no label row, the postprint reproduces only the BFI-2 (its only 'optimis-' hits are BFI item 9/19 and the Ferrando reference title), and Supplementary Tables SM10/SM11 hold scale-level correlations only; none of these carry LOT wording in Spanish. So item_text is the English LOT-R as its authors publish it (Carver's page), language=Spanish, _translated columns empty. Carver's page links 'A Spanish version of the LOT-R'; it was deliberately not used because it is off-source and nothing ties it to the Ferrando version this study cites -- a lead for a later backfill. (2) TRANSLATION_SOURCE=mixed: item_text = official_instrument_english (Carver's page, verbatim, straight apostrophe as served); option_text = study_supplied (the postprint's own English description of the scale, 'Respondents rate each item on a 4-point scale: 0 = strongly disagree, 1 = disagree, 2 = neutral, 3 = agree, and 4 = strongly agree'). (3) ANCHOR NUMBERING: the postprint numbers the anchors 0-4 (and calls five points a '4-point scale'); the deposit and live table store 1-5. Shipped as resp 1 = strongly disagree ... 5 = strongly agree. Direction verified, not assumed: keying LOT2/4/5 as 6-x gives scale M 3.330 / SD 0.826 / alpha 0.876 vs published 3.33 / 0.83 / .88; the high=disagree reading gives M 2.670. Carver's own A-E anchors ('I agree a lot' ... 'I DISagree a lot') are a different format and were NOT carried over; nor were his instructions, which belong to that letter format -- instructions blank because no instruction text is published for this administration. (4) MAPPING: reconstructed. LOT1..LOT6 are the deposit's own column names but carry no text; they are a 1-6 renumbering of LOT-R items 1,3,4,7,9,10 (the four fillers 2,5,6,8 are absent from the deposit). The tie rests on canonical order plus the study's own scoring key c(1,-1,1,-1,-1,1), which is exactly the LOT-R's opt/pess/opt/pess/pess/opt sequence. Verified PARTIAL (see verification_ and verify_ files): polarity class, raw storage and direction pinned; order within {LOT1,LOT3,LOT6} and within {LOT2,LOT4,LOT5} not. (5) RIGHTS: register verdict applied, not re-derived -- instrument_rights_register.csv 'Life Orientation Test-Revised (LOT-R)' = ship_with_note. Carver's page carries one caution: 'Please note that this is a research instrument, not intended for clinical applications.' It DISCLAIMS FITNESS (what the scale is good for) and reserves no right -- no fee, permission, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution term appears on the page; its only copyright line is the University of Miami site-wide footer 'Copyright: 2026 University of Miami. All Rights Reserved.', a notice about the website, not a term on the instrument -- so under the 2026-09-08 LOT-R ruling it does not block. The shipped wording is the originator's English, taken from the originator's own page. OSF deposit CC BY 4.0 governs the response data.
